content.html:
Key Takeaways
  • Fully-funded Master's degree (up to 2 years) at top US universities — covers tuition, travel, stipend, health insurance & more
  • Open to Nepali citizens with at least 3 years post-bachelor's full-time professional work experience in Nepal
  • No GRE or TOEFL needed at the application stage — shortlisted candidates take tests free of charge
  • Around 4,000 scholarships awarded globally each year across 160+ countries
  • 2027–28 cohort: Applications ran Feb 1 – May 31, 2026 (now closed) · Interviews: August 2026 · Program start: Fall 2027
  • All fields eligible except Medicine and Nursing — STEM and Business Management especially encouraged
  • All grantees must return to Nepal after completing the program (J-1 visa two-year home residency requirement)
⚠️
The 2027–28 application has closed According to USEF-Nepal, the 2027–28 Fulbright Foreign Student Program application opened on February 1, 2026 and closed on May 31, 2026 at 23:59 Eastern Time, with interviews in August 2026. The next call has not been announced, so watch usefnepal.org for the 2028–29 dates. Use this guide to prepare early, because the application window is only a few months long.

🎓What Is the Fulbright Foreign Student Program?

The Fulbright Foreign Student Program (FFSP) is the United States government's flagship international educational and cultural exchange initiative, administered globally by the Institute of International Education (IIE) and in Nepal by the U.S. Educational Foundation in Nepal (USEF-Nepal) — also known as the Fulbright Commission.

For Nepali students, the FFSP funds a fully-paid Master's degree at selected US universities. The program is designed to promote mutual understanding between Nepal and the US through the exchange of knowledge and professional talent. Since its inception, the global Fulbright Program has supported approximately 370,000 participants across more than 160 countries.

Selected participants for the 2027-28 cycle will begin their studies in Fall 2027. Candidates in STEM fields and Business Management are especially encouraged to apply.

💼Grant Benefits & What It Covers

The Fulbright FFSP is a comprehensive, fully-funded scholarship. Grantees pay nothing out of pocket — the program is designed so scholars can focus entirely on their academic and professional goals without financial worry.

🎓
Tuition & Academic Allowances Full tuition at a selected US university plus academic-related allowances
🏠
Living Stipend Monthly stipend to cover accommodation and daily living expenses
✈️
Round-Trip Travel Full international airfare from Nepal to the US and back
💊
Health Insurance Comprehensive medical insurance coverage for the grant period
🛂
J-1 & J-2 Visa Sponsorship Visa sponsorship for the grantee and eligible dependents (spouse or unmarried children under 21)
📚
Pre-Academic Training Enrichment seminars and pre-academic training specially designed for Fulbright grantees
🚀
Post-Degree Opportunities Post Degree Academic Training and post-study opportunities as per US immigration regulations
🌐
Global Alumni Network Induction into the Nepal and worldwide Fulbright alumni community
⚠️
J-1 Visa Two-Year Rule All grantees receive a J-1 exchange visitor visa, which requires returning to Nepal upon completing the academic program. Grantees are not eligible for a US immigrant visa, permanent residence, or certain non-immigrant work visas (H or L) until they have completed two years of home residency in Nepal after returning. This does not prevent travel to the US on other visa types during those two years.

✅Eligibility Requirements

To be considered for the Fulbright FFSP from Nepal, applicants must meet all of the following criteria as of the application deadline:

🇳🇵
Nepali Citizenship & Residence Must hold valid Nepali citizenship and be a current resident of Nepal at the time of applying.
💼
Work Experience (3 Years) At minimum 3 years of post-bachelor's full-time professional work in Nepal, directly relevant to the proposed field of study. A professional recommender must verify employment details.
🎓
16 Years of Formal Education A four-year bachelor's degree; OR a shorter bachelor's plus a completed Master's degree — such that total formal education equals at least 16 years.
📊
Academic Performance Minimum 60% aggregate marks or a 3.0/4.0 GPA in post-intermediate degrees. Score conversions between GPA and percentage are not permitted.
🗣️
English Proficiency Sufficient English to thrive in a US graduate program. TOEFL (100+) or GRE scores are only required after shortlisting — offered free by the Commission (August–September 2026).
🛂
US Visa Eligibility Must qualify for a non-immigrant J-1 US visa. Must not currently hold or be in the process of obtaining a US immigrant visa ("green card").

🚫Who Is NOT Eligible?

The following categories of applicants are automatically disqualified from the Fulbright FFSP from Nepal:

  • Individuals currently living, studying, or working outside Nepal at the time of application
  • Those who have resided in the United States for six months or more during the five years preceding the application deadline
  • Individuals who already hold a US degree (preference given to applicants without prior US or foreign study experience)
  • Students with a 3-year bachelor's who have completed only the first year of a 2-year Master's program
  • Master's students who have cleared all exams but have not yet fulfilled other university-mandated degree requirements
  • Students holding two or more 2-year/3-year bachelor's degrees but no Master's degree
  • Applicants seeking a degree in Medicine or Nursing
  • USEF-Nepal employees, local US Mission Nepal (Department of State) staff, and their spouses and dependent children — during employment and for one year after termination
ℹ️
Re-Application is Encouraged If you were not selected in a previous cycle, you are actively encouraged to re-apply. Strengthening your essays, gaining more relevant work experience, and refining your recommenders' letters can significantly improve your chances in subsequent cycles.

📋Required Documents Checklist

All applications are submitted online via the IIE portal — no hard copies are accepted. Prepare the following documents before you begin your application:

Application Section Document Required
CV / Résumé Maximum 2 pages, following the USEF-Nepal CV format
Academic Materials Attested copies of all diplomas/certificates and mark sheets/transcripts from SLC to most recent degree — arranged in reverse chronological order. Unattested materials will not be accepted.
Study Plan Essays Study/Research Objective (max 2 pages / 1,500 words) and Personal Statement (max 2 pages / 1,500 words). A Writing Sample is often required for Humanities and Social Sciences.
Identity Document Scanned copy of Nepali Citizenship Certificate, National ID, or Passport
Recommendations 3 letters of recommendation (professional and academic referees). Recommenders must submit directly online through the application system before the deadline.
Test Scores TOEFL/IELTS and GRE score reports — not mandatory at application stage. Prior valid scores may be submitted if available.
Work Sample (if applicable) Often required for study in the Arts, Communication, or Journalism fields
⚠️
Attestation Requirements Transcripts and certificates must be attested by the issuing institution, Government of Nepal, Tribhuvan University, Kathmandu University, or a government-approved notary public. USEF-Nepal also provides an attestation service (drop-off 10 AM–4 PM). You must bring originals along with clear photocopies, including the backside of all mark sheets.

📝Step-by-Step Application Process

The complete Fulbright application process is online through the IIE portal. Here is the full journey from start to grant notification:

1
Create Your IIE Application Account

Visit the USEF-Nepal website (usefnepal.org) and access the official IIE application portal. Sign up and start a new application for the 2027-28 FFSP cycle. No hard copies are accepted at any stage.

2
Gather & Attest All Academic Documents

Collect attested photocopies of all diplomas, certificates, and transcripts from SLC to your most recent degree, arranged in reverse chronological order. Drop originals at USEF-Nepal for attestation if needed (10 AM–4 PM).

3
Write Your Study/Research Objective

Clearly articulate your academic and career goals: what you aim to study, why you need a US Master's degree specifically, and what outcomes you intend to achieve. Maximum 2 pages or 1,500 words.

4
Write Your Personal Statement

Share your story — your strengths, key experiences, any challenges or inconsistencies in your academic or professional history, and how they have shaped your goals. Maximum 2 pages or 1,500 words.

5
Select & Brief Your Recommenders

Choose 3 recommenders (professional and academic) who know you well and can speak to your abilities. Your professional recommender must specifically verify your position, years of employment, and relevance to your proposed field. They submit online directly.

6
Identify Preferred US Universities

List at least 4 US institutions where you would like to study, aligned with your academic and professional goals. Research each university's program carefully before listing them.

7
Complete & Submit the Online Application

Fill in all sections of the IIE portal, review carefully for accuracy, acknowledge the plagiarism agreement, and submit before 11:59 pm Eastern Time on May 31, 2026. Late or incomplete applications are not accepted.

8
Initial Screening & Interview

Shortlisted candidates are notified and called for panel interviews in August 2026. Interviews evaluate your academic background, English communication skills, professional experience, and plans for contributing to Nepal after returning.

9
GRE & TOEFL Testing (Post-Interview)

Selected candidates take GRE and/or TOEFL tests in August–September 2026. These are offered free of charge by the Fulbright Commission. Prior valid test scores may be accepted.

10
Final Selection & Grant Award

Final nominees are forwarded to IIE in Washington for university placement. Only a small number of candidates from Nepal are selected each year. Successful grantees commence their programs in Fall 2027.

📅Official Application Timeline (2027–28 Cohort)

The official 2027-28 Fulbright FFSP timeline from USEF-Nepal is as follows:

February 1, 2026
Application Portal Opens. The IIE online application for the 2027-28 FFSP cycle becomes available. Access via USEF-Nepal's website.
May 31, 2026 — 11:59 PM Eastern Time
Application Deadline. All materials must be submitted online by this exact time. No late or partial submissions accepted. Recommenders must also submit by this date.
August 2026
Interviews. Shortlisted candidates are notified and invited for panel interviews conducted by the Fulbright Committee in Nepal.
August – September 2026
GRE & TOEFL Testing. Selected candidates take the required standardized tests, offered free of charge by the Commission.
Fall 2027
Program Commences. Final grantees begin their Master's degree studies at selected US universities.

🏆Key Elements of a Successful Application

The Fulbright Committee in Nepal selects only a small number of candidates each year — competition is intense. Based on official USEF-Nepal guidance and alumni insights, here is what separates winning applications:

Element 01
Follow All Instructions Precisely

Thoroughly review the application instructions. Double-check that all required documents are uploaded correctly, and answer every question with accuracy and completeness.

Element 02
Write a Specific Study Objective

Clearly articulate what you aim to study, your academic and career goals, and why a US Master's is specifically needed to achieve them. Vague or generic statements fail.

Element 03
Tell a Compelling Personal Story

Your Personal Statement should share your strengths, key experiences, and any inconsistencies in your academic/professional history — and how these shaped your goals.

Element 04
Demonstrate a Clear Return Plan

Fulbright values scholars who will return and contribute to Nepal. Describe concrete post-degree plans — a specific role, sector, or initiative you plan to pursue in Nepal.

Element 05
Choose Recommenders Strategically

Select referees who know you well and can provide unique, well-rounded insights. Brief them on what to emphasize. In US culture, the content of a recommendation matters more than the referee's title.

Element 06
Provide Complete Academic History

List all postsecondary institutions in reverse chronological order. Include all academic, professional, and personal awards and honors received.

Element 07
List At Least 4 US Universities

Research programs that align with your academic and professional goals and list at least four institutions. Specific, well-researched choices signal seriousness and fit.

Element 08
Review AI & Plagiarism Policies

Be aware that individual universities may have AI usage guidelines. Carefully read and agree to the Fulbright plagiarism policy. Plagiarism results in immediate disqualification.

❓Frequently Asked Questions

When does the Fulbright FFSP application open and close for Nepal?+
The 2027-28 application opened on February 1, 2026 and closed at 11:59 PM Eastern Time on May 31, 2026. The application is submitted entirely online via the IIE portal — no hard copies accepted.
Do I need GRE or TOEFL scores to apply?+
No. GRE and TOEFL scores are not required at the application stage. If you are shortlisted following the interview (August 2026), the Fulbright Commission will ask you to take these tests in August–September 2026 — offered free of charge. If you have valid prior test scores, you may submit them voluntarily.
How much work experience do I need to apply from Nepal?+
You need at least 3 years of post-bachelor's full-time professional work experience in Nepal, directly relevant to your proposed field of study. This experience must be verified by a professional recommender who outlines your position(s) and duration. Experience across multiple organizations counts as long as the total meets the minimum.
Can I apply if I am currently living, studying, or working outside Nepal?+
No. You must be a current resident of Nepal at the time of application. Individuals who have resided in the United States for 6 months or more in the five years preceding the application deadline are also ineligible.
Can I apply if I already hold a Master's degree?+
Yes. You are eligible to apply even if you already hold a Master's degree, as long as all other eligibility criteria are fully met.
Which documents need to be attested and how?+
All academic diplomas, certificates, and mark sheets/transcripts must be officially attested. Attestation can be done by the issuing institution, Government of Nepal, Tribhuvan University, Kathmandu University, a government-approved notary public, or directly at USEF-Nepal (10 AM–4 PM). Work experience letters do not require attestation.
Can I convert my GPA to percentage or vice versa?+
No. You are not permitted to convert between grading systems. If your bachelor's and master's degrees use different systems (e.g., one uses percentage and the other uses GPA), you must meet the minimum requirement for each degree separately under its respective grading system.
Which fields of study can I pursue under the Fulbright FFSP?+
Almost any field is eligible — Engineering, Business, Social Sciences, Arts, STEM, and more. Medicine and Nursing are the only excluded fields. Candidates in STEM and Business Management are especially encouraged to apply.
What is the J-1 two-year home residency requirement?+
All Fulbright grantees receive a J-1 exchange visitor visa which legally requires them to return to Nepal upon completing their program. They are not eligible for a US immigrant visa, permanent residency, or certain non-immigrant work visas (H or L) until they have completed two years of residence in Nepal after returning. This does not prevent travel to the US on other visa categories during those two years.
Can I re-apply if I was rejected in a previous year?+
Absolutely — and the Fulbright Commission actively encourages it. Many successful grantees applied more than once. Use each cycle to strengthen your essays, gain more relevant work experience, and refine your application based on feedback.

📞Contact & Official Resources

For the most accurate and up-to-date information, always refer directly to USEF-Nepal (the official Fulbright Commission in Nepal). Be cautious of unofficial sources.
